grounding.derivation: The implementation persists an FSM snapshot, records snapshot metadata, compacts logs, and later sends a snapshot to lagging peers. The documentation states that snapshots permit removal of logs used to reach the captured state and that committed entries may be applied to the FSM.
grounding.applicability: Applicable when snapshotting is enabled, a snapshot is successfully created and persisted, and compaction or lagging-peer recovery is exercised.

alternatives: The selected store may provide stronger atomicity or recovery guarantees than the interfaces express.

claims.description: For every successful takeSnapshot path, log deletion must not remove the only recoverable history or snapshot representation needed to reconstruct the FSM state at or before the compacted index and to continue replication.

scope.description: The successful path from Raft.takeSnapshot through SnapshotSink.Close, last-snapshot publication, compactLogs, and later sendLatestSnapshot.
assumptions: The snapshot metadata index identifies the state represented by the persisted snapshot.

excluded: Failure behavior of concrete stores not included in the supplied materials.

grounding.derivation: takeSnapshot calls FSMSnapshot.Persist, closes the sink, updates last-snapshot state, and then compacts through compactLogsWithTrailing. A lagging peer is later recovered through sendLatestSnapshot, which selects and opens a listed snapshot. These producer-consumer dependencies make recoverability across compaction an applicable candidate obligation.
grounding.applicability: Applicable only after successful snapshot persistence and close; not established for error paths or concrete stores whose contracts are unread.
unresolved: Whether sink.Close durably publishes the snapshot before compaction.
Whether List returns a snapshot that Open can still recover after compaction.
Whether the FSM snapshot is semantically complete at snapReq.index.
alternatives: TrailingLogs may preserve sufficient incremental history even if snapshot recovery is unavailable, but this is not established.
